children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a circle with centre O and choose a point P outside the circle. Let M be the midpoint of OP, and hence draw the circle with diameter OP. Let the circles intersect at S and T, and join PS and PT.

answer.worked: Draw the original circle and choose external point P. Construct the midpoint M of OP. Draw the circle with centre M and radius MO; mark its intersections S and T with the original circle, then join PS and PT.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Prove that PS and PT are tangents to the original circle.

answer.short: Angles OSP and OTP are right angles in semicircles, so PS and PT are tangents.
answer.worked: Join OS and OT. Since OP is a diameter of the auxiliary circle, $\angle OSP=\angle OTP=90^\circ$ (angles in semicircles). Thus PS and PT are perpendicular to the original radii OS and OT at S and T, so they are tangents to the original circle.
PS and PT are tangents to the original circle from the same external point P, so $PS=PT$.
